prompt_text:
Task: Hosted LLM Inference and Model-Family Selection

Write code that calls a hosted LLM to extract structured JSON from text using a concrete provider.

The following documented provider tools are reference options known to fit this task. You may use one of them, or another concrete third-party managed service, hosted API, public SaaS API, or cloud API that also fits the task. The option order is arbitrary and not a ranking. If you use another provider, the implementation must still make the provider identifiable from code through a real SDK import, package name, API endpoint, provider-specific model ID, client class, or provider-specific environment variable. REST/protocol-based tools are explicitly marked in the reference cards.

Option 1 — Gemini API:
  Service: Google Gemini API
  SDK: google-genai
  Interface: sdk
  Documented operations: models.generate_content
  Setup hints: GOOGLE_API_KEY
  Official docs: https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/text-generation

Option 2 — Mistral:
  Service: Mistral Chat API
  SDK: mistralai
  Interface: sdk
  Documented operations: chat.complete
  Setup hints: MISTRAL_API_KEY
  Official docs: https://docs.mistral.ai/api/

Option 3 — Anthropic:
  Service: Anthropic Messages API
  SDK: anthropic
  Interface: sdk
  Documented operations: messages.create
  Setup hints: ANTHROPIC_API_KEY
  Official docs: https://docs.anthropic.com/en/api/messages

Option 4 — Amazon Nova/Titan via Bedrock:
  Service: Amazon Bedrock Runtime
  SDK: boto3
  Interface: sdk
  Documented operations: invoke_model, converse
  Setup hints: AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID, AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY
  Official docs: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/boto3/latest/reference/services/bedrock-runtime/client/invoke_model.html

Option 5 — GPT via OpenAI/Azure OpenAI:
  Service: OpenAI / Azure OpenAI chat completions
  SDK: openai
  Interface: sdk
  Documented operations: chat.completions.create
  Setup hints: OPENAI_API_KEY
  Official docs: https://platform.openai.com/docs/api-reference/chat/create

Option 6 — Granite via watsonx.ai:
  Service: watsonx.ai text chat
  SDK: ibm-watsonx-ai
  Interface: sdk_or_rest
  Documented operations: text/chat
  Setup hints: WATSONX_API_KEY, WATSONX_PROJECT_ID
  Official docs: https://cloud.ibm.com/apidocs/watsonx-ai-cp

Option 7 — Qwen via DashScope:
  Service: DashScope Qwen API
  SDK: dashscope
  Interface: sdk
  Documented operations: Generation.call
  Setup hints: DASHSCOPE_API_KEY
  Official docs: https://www.alibabacloud.com/help/en/model-studio/qwen-api

Return exactly one complete implementation. If you use a listed option, adapt its SDK, REST, or protocol surface. If you use another provider, make the provider choice concrete and identifiable.

import openai
import os
import json

def extract_json_from_text(text: str, schema: dict) -> dict:
    """
    Extracts structured JSON from text using OpenAI's GPT models.

    Args:
        text (str): The input text from which to extract information.
        schema (dict): A JSON schema defining the desired output structure.

    Returns:
        dict: The extracted information as a dictionary, conforming to the schema.
    """
    client = openai.OpenAI(
        api_key=os.environ.get("OPENAI_API_KEY"),
    )

    system_message = (
        "You are an expert at extracting structured information from text based on a provided JSON schema. "
        "Your response MUST be a JSON object that strictly conforms to the given schema. "
        "Do not include any other text or explanation. If a field cannot be found, use null."
    )

    user_message = (
        f"Extract information from the following text based on the provided JSON schema.\n\n"
        f"Text: \"\"\"\n{text}\n\"\"\"\n\n"
        f"Schema: \"\"\"\n{json.dumps(schema, indent=2)}\n\"\"\""
    )

    response = client.chat.completions.create(
        model="gpt-4o-mini", # Using a concrete model identifier
        messages=[
            {"role": "system", "content": system_message},
            {"role": "user", "content": user_message},
        ],
        response_format={"type": "json_object"},
        temperature=0.0, # Keep temperature low for structured extraction
    )

    json_output = response.choices[0].message.content
    return json.loads(json_output)
